newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up, with all contracts above 20,000 yuan, on Wednesday due to short-covering and short-term speculative buying, traders said.
The most active March 1997 contract ended at 20,070 yuan ($2,418) per tonne, rising 340 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 19,900 and hit a high of 20,100.
December rose 80 to 20,230, January 220 to 20,100, February 340 to 20,080, April 380 to 20,090, May 390 to 20,150 and June 250 to 20,100.
Combined volume fell to 64,680 tonnes from 107,720.

Copper opened higher on short-covering and short-term speculative buying triggered by overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange and rose further before most contracts closed at or near their intra-day highs.
"The fact that all contracts ended above the key 20,000-yuan level again indicated long position holders have not lost their confidence," one trader said.
"Copper will fluctuate in a wide range in the next few days," a second trader said. "Today's movement was only a beginning."
Traders said copper was likely to move around the 20,000-yuan level in the next few days.
Aluminium ended little changed. The December contract was unchanged at 13,700 yuan per tonne, January did not trade and February was unchanged at 14,000.
Combined volume fell to 400 tonnes from 420.
